question: What does sustainability mean in the context of healthcare quality improvement?

options.A: An external audit conducted once a year
options.B: A temporary project with fixed funding
options.C: A short-term trial of new equipment
options.D: A permanent change integrated into daily routine

explanation: Sustainability ensures that a new clinical practice becomes standard operating procedure rather than fading away. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why do many well-planned healthcare interventions fail to last over time?

options.B: Lack of permanent integration into daily ward routines
options.C: Too much focus on long-term patient outcomes
options.D: Excessive involvement of frontline nursing staff

explanation: Initiatives fail when they are treated as temporary projects rather than permanent shifts in daily clinical workflow. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h1)

question: What is slippage in clinical quality improvement?

options.A: The gradual return to old practices after a project ends
options.B: The intentional removal of safety checklists from wards
options.C: A sudden strike by hospital nurses over poor pay
options.D: An immediate failure of newly purchased medical equipment

explanation: Slippage describes how behaviors slowly drift backward toward familiar routines once active project monitoring stops. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h2)

question: Improvement fatigue in a hospital ward is usually caused by which of the following?

options.A: Allowing nurses to design their own work schedules
options.B: Introducing too many changes at the same time
options.C: Sticking rigidly to one safe procedure for years
options.D: Providing too much constructive feedback on data

explanation: Constant overlapping directives overwhelm personnel, turning valuable interventions into exhausting burdens. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which strategy directly helps embed a new practice into the physical ward environment?

options.A: Placing visual reminder posters at the point of care
options.B: Removing all operational manuals from the ward
options.C: Waiting for annual nursing board evaluations
options.D: Punishing staff who forget the new guidelines

explanation: Environmental cues like posters or checklists serve as direct prompts for staff during busy clinical shifts. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h3)

question: Why is workflow alignment crucial when introducing a new clinical practice?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any staff training sessions
options.B: It makes the new behavior easier to perform than the old one
options.C: It guarantees that funding for the project will increase
options.D: It ensures that doctors take over all nursing administrative tasks

explanation: If a new practice requires fewer cumbersome steps than the old habit, staff will adopt it naturally. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is a key feature of a just culture in healthcare?

options.A: Punishing every mistake severely to prevent repetition
options.B: Leaving all disciplinary actions to external regulatory bodies
options.C: Encouraging the open reporting of clinical errors without fear
options.D: Ignoring minor protocol violations during busy night shifts

explanation: A just culture supports transparency so teams can learn from mistakes rather than hiding them. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h4)

question: Capacity building in nursing staff primarily aims to achieve what outcome?

options.A: Reducing the total number of employed nurses in the facility
options.B: Equipping staff with skills to lead future audits and mentor others
options.C: Preventing nurses from participating in quality projects
options.D: Shifting all administrative ward duties away from the hospital

explanation: Building internal capacity ensures that the facility can maintain improvements independently over the long term. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of continuous data monitoring in clinical settings?

options.A: To replace direct patient bedside assessment
options.B: To penalize wards with low patient admission numbers
options.C: To prevent silent regression in clinical performance
options.D: To compile unnecessary paperwork for ministry officials

explanation: Regular data tracking catches drops in compliance early before old bad habits completely return. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h5)

question: How should quality improvement data be shared with frontline nursing staff?

options.A: Presented simply and discussed in regular team meetings
options.B: Kept strictly confidential among senior hospital directors
options.C: Published only in international medical research journals
options.D: Given out once every five years during license renewal

explanation: Sharing relevant data directly with the team helps them see their impact and motivates continued adherence. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h5)
